---
title: "P5 exercise — Evaluate a physiological intervention"
---

Use the [tutorial](index.qmd). Allow 60–75 minutes, including a short group
discussion. All evidence records and numeric trial results below are invented
for this exercise. They are not copied from a database or a published study.
No transformation, culture or release activity is requested.

## 1. Explain survival versus performance

A fictional line closes stomata earlier during drying. It retains more leaf
water but makes fewer seeds under one drought regime. Draw a mechanism linking
the intervention to both observations. What additional measurements would test
the carbon-gain and leaf-temperature explanations? Could the same response be
beneficial under a more severe regime? Define the outcome before saying “better”.

## 2. Separate annotation from evidence

Use this offline record; an optional comparison with a real
[TAIR](https://www.arabidopsis.org/) entry can be made if access is available.

| Field | Fictional record |
| --- | --- |
| Identifier | TEACH-GC1 (invented; not a TAIR locus) |
| Annotation | Candidate membrane transport regulator |
| Expression | Reporter detected mainly in guard cells under tested conditions |
| Perturbation | One transformed line has earlier closure |
| Similarity | Related sequence in another species has an annotated transport role |

Rank the claims: observed reporter location; proven native-protein location;
proven causal control of closure; plausible mechanistic hypothesis. Which
evidence is direct and which is inferred? Explain why searching a gene name
and copying the first description would lose essential uncertainty.

## 3. Design controls before interpreting a transformed line

The line in task 2 was regenerated through tissue culture. Propose appropriate
background and culture controls, multiple independent events and a way to
test association with the intended change. Explain what a tissue-specific
promoter is intended to achieve and why its specificity needs measurement.
Distinguish stable transformation, transient expression and editing.

## 4. Read a small factorial comparison

The following invented means are seeds per plant from equally sized groups;
variation and replication details have deliberately not been supplied.

| Line | No herbivores | Herbivores present |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Control | 100 | 50 |
| Defence-enhanced | 85 | 75 |

Calculate the line difference in each environment. Explain how the pattern
could reflect a defence cost and protection benefit. List the missing design
and uncertainty information needed before recommending the line. Do not infer
statistical significance from four means.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Direction check

Enhanced minus control is −15 seeds without herbivores and +25 with herbivores.
The pattern is condition-dependent. It does not establish the molecular
mechanism, the long-term field effect or significance.
:::

## 5. Write a reasoned recommendation

Choose either fictional intervention and write 250–350 words addressing its
mechanism, intended setting, evidence, limitations and next measurement. Include
one potential benefit, one context-specific ecological concern and one question
of access or decision power. Identify at least one empirical question and one
value judgement. Compare with a stated alternative rather than an unspecified
“natural” plant. A recommendation to collect more evidence is valid if you name
the evidence and explain how it would affect the decision.

## Completion check

Keep physiological, empirical and ethical reasoning connected. A label such
as “GM”, “natural” or “stress-tolerant” does not supply a complete evaluation.
Finish with the [self-check](quiz.qmd).
